title: Localization of the ordinary scheme evaluation equation
statement: Let Y be a scheme, Q its derived localization and H its derived internal Hom. For arbitrary complexes P,F, let O be the degree-zero unit and V=Hom(P,O). Define c_M:Q Hom(P,M) to H(QP,QM) by applying Hom(P,-) to the fixed K-injective augmentation and then the inverse localization factorization. For isomorphisms eK:QP to K, eN:QF to N and an ordinary evaluation f:Tot(F tensor V) to Hom(P,F) satisfying the component predicate [def-pc-scheme-ordinary-evaluation-formula], the canonical tensor-Hom bijection [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] sends (eN inverse tensor identity);mu;Qf;c_F;H(eK inverse,eN) to associator;N tensor uncurrying of (c_O;H(eK inverse,QO to 1));right unitor. The map QO to 1 is the inverse quotient comparison at O. This is only a morphism equation: it assumes no Hom-exactness, no K-flatness of V and no K-injectivity of F, and asserts no comparison is invertible.

proof.text: Expose the canonical three-variable naturality field. Extend the representative equation to any tensor-source complex by a K-flat resolution. The canonical representative witness is equal to the explicit uncurrying map by tensor-summand extensionality; naturality of explicit localized uncurrying identifies the resolution composite, and cancellation of Q of the resolution tensor identity removes the K-flatness assumption.

Apply the extended representative formula to f followed by Hom(P,eta_F), and to Hom(P,eta_O). Apply canonical naturality along the tensor model comparison and eK,eN. Substitute the explicit ordinary uncurrying calculation. Associator naturality, tensor functoriality, right-unitor naturality and eN.inv_hom_id prove the final transport equation.

theorem schemeOrdinaryEvaluation_localization (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (K N : schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (P F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (eK : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ K) (eN : DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ N)
    (f : pullbackTensorTotal Y F
        (homComplex.{u, u, u, u} (R := Y.sheaf) P
          ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
            (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))))) ⟶
      homComplex.{u, u, u, u} (R := Y.sheaf) P F)
    (hf : IsSchemeOrdinaryEvaluation Y P F f) :
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.sheaf
    let O := (HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).obj
      (𝟙_ (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)))
    let V := homComplex.{u, u, u, u} (R := Y.sheaf) P O
    let c := schemeOrdinaryHomComparison Y P F ≫ H.map (eK.inv.op, eN.hom)
    let d := schemeOrdinaryHomComparison Y P O ≫
      H.map (eK.inv.op, ((DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso _).app O).inv)
    schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv Y (N ⊗ DerivedCategory.Q.obj V) K N
        ((eN.inv ▷ DerivedCategory.Q.obj V) ≫ pullbackTensorModelMap Y F V ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map f ≫ c) =
      (α_ N (DerivedCategory.Q.obj V) K).hom ≫ N ◁
        (schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv Y (DerivedCategory.Q.obj V) K
          (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory Y)) d) ≫ (ρ_ N).hom
